forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.committee: Adult Care and Health Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: ACH26-040A Dom Care Contract Award (PART 1) - ACH PDS 09.09.26
findings.headline: Delegated authority to move providers between Tier 2 and Tier 1 creates price risk that must be absorbed within Adult Social Care departmental budget
findings.detail: The council grants delegated authority to the Director of Adult Social Care to move providers from Tier 2 (general framework) to Tier 1 (patch providers) via a reserve list mechanism. The paper identifies that unit prices may differ between tiers, and any cost increase from such movement must be managed within the director's existing budgetary envelope.
findings.matters: Identifies a discretionary spending risk within an already-committed departmental budget, requiring cost absorption if tier-movement decisions result in higher unit prices
findings.quote: There is some financial risk arising from the seeking of delegated authority to move providers from Tier 2 to Tier 1 as the unit price tendered might be different. If the price is higher, the risk shall be managed by the Director of Adult Social Care within their budgetary envelope.

findings.committee: Adult Care and Health Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: ACH26-040A Dom Care Contract Award (PART 1) - ACH PDS 09.09.26
findings.headline: Framework contract contains no inflation until April 2028, then rises by CPI annually, providing two-year cost stability in a four-year commitment
findings.detail: The domiciliary care framework does not include contractual inflation adjustment until April 2028. From that point, prices will rise annually by CPI, currently assumed at government target of 2% per annum. This provides fixed costs for the initial two years of the four-year contract.
findings.matters: Provides cost stability in a large recurring service contract and aligns future inflation to government target-level CPI
findings.figures: No inflation until April 2028, thereafter 2% CPI assumed annually
findings.quote: There is some inflationary risk mitigation in that there is no contractual inflation to be applied until April 2028.

findings.committee: Adult Care and Health Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: ACH26-040A Dom Care Contract Award (PART 1) - ACH PDS 09.09.26
findings.headline: Council confirms adequate budgetary provision for £20.3m annual domiciliary care contract while identifying demand-led service risks to be managed within departmental budgets
findings.detail: The council states there is adequate budgetary provision across Adult Services (£18.8m) and Children's Services (£1.5m) for the new framework. However, it explicitly identifies that risks from demand-led spending will be managed by respective directors to ensure their departmental budgets outturn within the agreed envelope.
findings.matters: Shows council's governance mechanism for managing volatility and cost exposure in a major recurring demand-led service budget
findings.figures: £18.8m Adult Social Care budget, £1.5m Children's Social Care budget, total £20.3m annual
findings.quote: There are risks to the budget arising from it being a demand led service. Such risks shall be managed by the respective Directors to ensure that their departmental budgets as a whole outturn within the budgetary envelope.

findings.committee: Adult Care and Health Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: ACH26-037 Appendix A - Transformation and Improvement - ACH PDS 09.09.26
findings.headline: £906,000 of £1.830m recurring savings target delivered as of July 2026, with March 2027 deadline
findings.detail: The Adult Services Transformation and Improvement Programme reports £906,000 of recurring savings delivered by July 2026 against a target of £1.830m by March 2027. Identified contributions include £631,000 from optimised care and support packages and £268,000 from the front door redesign. The programme reports green status across most constituent projects and is described as 'on track' and 'progressing as planned'.
findings.matters: Finance directors and lenders track delivery against committed savings targets in Medium Term Financial Plans; shortfalls require budget adjustment or reserve drawdown, while delivery on track confirms programme discipline and the council's ability to execute its financial plan.
findings.figures: £906,000 delivered as of July 2026; £1.830m target by March 2027; £631,000 from optimised care and support packages; £268,000 from front door redesign
findings.quote: As of July 2026, the Programme has delivered £906,000 of recurring savings against a target of £1.830m by March 2027

findings.committee: Adult Care and Health Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: ACH26-037 Adult Services Transformation and Improvement Update Report - ACH PDS 09.09.26
findings.headline: Programme in year three; Strategic Delivery Partner contract with Social Care Institute for Excellence concluded
findings.detail: The council is four months into the third year of the programme, described as firmly established and delivering significant service improvements. The SCIE contract for external delivery support has concluded, with the programme having embedded the approaches, tools, and capabilities developed during the partnership.
findings.matters: Transition from external expert support to internal delivery is a sustainability checkpoint; if capabilities have not been properly embedded, the council faces risk to programme delivery and unanticipated costs for alternative support
findings.figures: Year 3 of programme; SCIE contract concluded
findings.quote: The Strategic Delivery Partner contract with the Social Care Institute for Excellence (SCIE), which provided expert supported to Adult Service's Transformation and Improvement Programme during the previous year, has now concluded.
